supporting_pages.title: "Analytics metrics, dimensions, and filters reference \_|\_ Apigee \_|\_\
evidence_snippets: For example, policy error metrics, grouped by the developer app dimension, might help you discover that an API key or OAuth token has expired for a given app; or you might find that a specific API proxy is throwing a lot of SpikeArrest policy errors, leading you to discover that the proxy's spike arrest limit doesn't account for an increase in holiday traffic.

In order to get this dimension, app developers or AppGroups must have apps associated with one or more API products that contain the API proxies being called, and the proxies must check for an API key or OAuth token sent with the API call.

supporting_pages.title: Method: organizations.apps.list \_|\_ Apigee \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: The filter expression to be used to get the list of apps, where filtering can be done on developerEmail, apiProduct, consumerKey, status, appId, appName, appType and appGroup.
Lists IDs of apps within an organization that have the specified app status (approved or revoked) or are of the specified app type (developer or company).

Resource path of the parent in the following format: organizations/{org} Authorization requires the following IAM permission on the specified resource parent : apigee.apps.list Query parameters Parameters status string Optional.

supporting_pages.title: Rate-limiting \_|\_ Apigee \_|\_ Google Cloud Documentation
evidence_snippets: To maintain performance and availability across a diverse base of client apps, it's critical to maintain app traffic within the limits of the capacity of your APIs and backend services.
Quota policy This policy enforces consumption limits on client apps by maintaining a distributed 'counter' that tallies incoming requests.
The counter can tally API calls for any identifiable entity, including apps, developers, API keys, access tokens, and so on.
